notes: Read SKILL.md in full (the only file). Linux performance tuning: a measure-change-one-thing-measure methodology, monitoring tools (mpstat, vmstat, iostat, perf), sysctl network/memory profiles, I/O scheduler and read-ahead, CPU governor, fio/sysbench/iperf3 benchmarking, and web/database tuning profiles.

Medium because following it changes host configuration as root: writing /etc/sysctl.d files and `sysctl --system` (SKILL.md:80-172), echoing to /sys for I/O scheduler and CPU governor, writing a udev rule and a systemd unit and enabling them (193-248), and `apt/dnf install -y` of fio, sysbench, iperf3 from distro repositories (260-300). Acceptable: tuning the host is the user's request, the skill requires baseline measurement and changing one parameter at a time with revert if not beneficial (33-40), and nothing disables security controls or deletes data.

Users should apply settings deliberately: the database profile's `vm.overcommit_memory = 2` (SKILL.md:339) can make allocations fail, disabling turbo and forcing the `performance` governor raise power use, and fio write tests create 1 GB files per job in the working directory. Related Skills (SKILL.md:362-365) are named by plain text only.
